+# One decision method, optional specialist enrichment
+
+Every ASDG role can use the shared Decision method. A specialist needs a local method only when recurring domain guidance adds value.
+This is instruction-level dispatch: the shared skill explicitly reads the local file; folder placement does not create a native runtime override.
+
+![The shared Decision skill checks the active specialist's folder, uses its optional local method or generic defaults, then returns a common decision result.](images/decision-specialization.svg)
+
+## Resolve the method
+
+Use the selected specialist or explicit role assignment to find its canonical `folder` in the existing agent catalogue.
+Check exactly `<folder>/skills/decision/SKILL.md`, relative to the bound client root, independently of the terminal working directory.
+If present, read it and its required references once, then continue the shared workflow with its enrichments. The local method must not recursively invoke the shared entrypoint.
+If absent, apply the generic method using the task, domain evidence and role contract; absence is normal and creates no file or warning.
+With no selected or assigned role, use the generic method provisionally; do not invent a specialist or change Focus.
+If a local file exists but is invalid, cannot be read or contradicts the shared contract, report the specific gap; do not silently treat it as absent.
+
+## Shared interface and extension points
+
+Input is the current decision, project, role, requested action, constraints, evidence and explicit human choices.
+The shared workflow owns purpose, alternatives, evidence distinctions, recommendation/selection, consequences and revisit conditions.
+
+| Optional local enrichment | What the specialist supplies |
+| --- | --- |
+| Frame the decision | Domain responsibilities and relevant alternatives. |
+| Evaluate alternatives | Domain criteria, evidence requirements and common analytical mistakes. |
+| Explain the result | Useful domain visuals and details within the shared documentation standard. |
+| Revisit the choice | Domain-specific changes or observations that warrant reassessment. |
+
+Unspecified extension points inherit generic behavior. A local method need not repeat the common workflow or implement every extension point.
+Every method returns the same decision meaning: rationale, comparable options, evidence/uncertainty, choice status, consequences and revisit conditions.
+Return analysis or save authorized documentation according to the request and owning contract; neither the method nor its result approves execution.
+
+## Maintaining a specialization
+
+Use a real `skills/decision/SKILL.md` folder/file with YAML-first `name: decision` and a domain-specific description.
+This is a role-local resource loaded by the shared entrypoint, not another globally registered `$asdg-decision` command.
+A specialist may propose enrichment when the generic method is insufficient; create or update it within an authorized methodology-maintenance task.
+Keep only meaningful differences, link domain foundations, and test the changed behavior. Do not generate empty methods for every role.
+Local methods may refine criteria and presentation but cannot remove shared evidence obligations, change Focus, widen writes, or alter approval rules.
+The [architecture specialization](../../05-high-level-design-and-architecture/skills/decision/SKILL.md) demonstrates this extension point; other roles may keep the generic method.

+---
+name: decision
+description: Enrich the shared ASDG Decision method with high-level architecture criteria, evidence and explanatory views.
+---
+
+# Architecture decision specialization
+
+Owner: ASDG-05. Apply this local method after the shared [Decision workflow](../../../skills/asdg-decision/SKILL.md) has resolved this role.
+Inherit its common method and [extension contract](../../../skills/asdg-decision/specialization.md); do not invoke the shared entrypoint recursively.
+Read [architecture foundations](../../docs/architectural-decisions.md) and the [role contract](../../types/contract.md).
+
+## Frame and compare
+
+Identify the system responsibility being allocated: boundaries, deployment, interfaces, data/control ownership, resilience or a dependency.
+Compare alternative ways to fulfill that responsibility; distinguish complementary layers from competing choices.
+Use relevant latency, reliability, consistency, security, operability, cost, portability and migration effort; explain which qualities drive this decision.
+Include the current architecture when viable and prefer a commitment proportionate to the current outcome and change cost.
+
+## Evidence and explanation
+
+Connect alternatives to use cases, constraints, existing implementation and evaluation findings; a feature list or vendor identity does not demonstrate fitness.
+Keep measured behavior distinct from intended architecture and untested expectations; identify the smallest useful evidence gap.
+Choose a component, sequence, deployment or failure-boundary view that reveals responsibilities and consequences.
+Use the shared short visual package for assigned architecture documentation within the role contract's existing paths.
+
+## Reconsideration
+
+Name concrete changes in load, failure tolerance, deployment, ownership, integration or user needs that would reopen the choice.
+Distinguish a missing implementation of the selected design from evidence that the design itself is unsuitable.
+All unmentioned behavior inherits the generic method. This specialization grants no additional write, implementation or acceptance authority.

+# A shared decision method with optional specialization
+
+Every ASDG specialist now uses the common Decision method. A local skill adds domain judgment when useful; specialists that need no customization keep the generic behavior.
+
+![The shared skill checks the active specialist folder and combines an optional local method or generic defaults with a common decision result.](../../../asdg/skills/asdg-decision/images/decision-specialization.svg)
+
+## What changed
+
+The [shared workflow](../../../asdg/skills/asdg-decision/SKILL.md) resolves the role through the existing catalogue and checks its `skills/decision/SKILL.md`.
+The [specialization contract](../../../asdg/skills/asdg-decision/specialization.md) defines optional enrichment of framing, criteria, evidence, visuals and revisit conditions.
+Missing local methods are normal. Existing but unreadable or conflicting methods are reported explicitly; another role's method is never silently substituted.
+The [ASDG-05 local method](../../../asdg/05-high-level-design-and-architecture/skills/decision/SKILL.md) connects architectural criteria to its existing foundations. Other roles use the generic method.
+Shared guidance applies across ASDG; the role's existing contract still governs documentation destination and authority.
+This is explicit instruction-level dispatch, independent of terminal working directory. It introduces no Python class hierarchy, extra public command or automatic role activation.
+
+## Validation
+
+Both shared and local skills pass the skill syntax validator. The structural verifier and whitespace checks pass.
+All 28 portable tests and 3 agent-configuration tests pass; a new regression verifies generic roles need no placeholder and optional local methods survive repeat setup from a specialist subdirectory.
+The new diagram and updated guidance were rendered within a 720 px document pane, with images displayed at 656 px; the shared-interface page was visually inspected.
+An independent read-only exercise loaded ASDG-05's local method and used generic fallback for ASDG-04, with domain-appropriate criteria and unchanged hashes across 424 fixture files.
+Its reported architecture-entry link concern was checked: the relative link correctly resolves inside `asdg/` to an existing shared skill; no repair was needed.
+The full package checker retains eight pre-existing external presentation-link failures in unchanged `asdg/README.md`; no other issues were reported.
+
+## Scope and evidence
+
+This authorized methodology update preserves application files, role permissions, catalogue identity, project/sprint/lifecycle state and previous review history.
+No placeholder overrides were created for other specialists. Creating a future override remains methodology maintenance, separate from using Decision on a client task.
+The [technical receipt](02.4-review-decision-specialization.json) records exact changes, checks and limitations. Fresh native role invocation and runtime enforcement are not established by these tests.
